title: IFC1: implicit-fiber four-input collimation with streamed, unstored pair fibers, T and Q = O(poly(n) 2^((29/20) sqrt n)), S_C = O(n^2 2^(sqrt n)) and O(n) qubits

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single IFC1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (e-man07's CW1 algorithm, public submission cfe82a87, with its collimation tree replaced by the schedule of proof.md Section 7: binary linear merges up to tables of length 2^(kappa+1+w) with w = ceil(sqrt n), and above them four-input merges MERGE4I whose pair fibers are streamed by class-restricted Schroeppel-Shamir heaps rather than stored as tables; free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap, and exhaustive search for n < 1024; specified in full in proof.md) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its total charged sequential work is T(N,s) = O(n^4 (log2 n)^2 2^((29/20) sqrt n)), with the uniform bit-length envelope B_T(n) = n^4 (log2 n)^2 2^((29/20) sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. The inner coefficient 29/20 is an explicit rational, not an unknown big-O constant: the proof bounds the tree height by tau sqrt n + 4 with tau = sqrt 6 - 1 < 29/20. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single IFC1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (e-man07's CW1 algorithm, public submission cfe82a87, with its collimation tree replaced by the schedule of proof.md Section 7: binary linear merges up to tables of length 2^(kappa+1+w) with w = ceil(sqrt n), and above them four-input merges MERGE4I whose pair fibers are streamed by class-restricted Schroeppel-Shamir heaps rather than stored as tables; free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap, and exhaustive search for n < 1024; specified in full in proof.md) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak classical workspace is S_C(N,s) = O(n^2 2^(sqrt n)) bits, with envelope B_C(n) = n^2 2^(sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. The inner coefficient is explicit, not an unknown big-O constant. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single IFC1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (e-man07's CW1 algorithm, public submission cfe82a87, with its collimation tree replaced by the schedule of proof.md Section 7: binary linear merges up to tables of length 2^(kappa+1+w) with w = ceil(sqrt n), and above them four-input merges MERGE4I whose pair fibers are streamed by class-restricted Schroeppel-Shamir heaps rather than stored as tables; free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap, and exhaustive search for n < 1024; specified in full in proof.md) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, its peak quantum workspace is S_Q(N,s) = O(n) qubits, with envelope B_Q(n) = n, whose exact growth index is 0. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For every N >= 2 and every s in Z/NZ, with n = ceil(log2 N), the single IFC1 algorithm and configuration of proof.md (e-man07's CW1 algorithm, public submission cfe82a87, with its collimation tree replaced by the schedule of proof.md Section 7: binary linear merges up to tables of length 2^(kappa+1+w) with w = ceil(sqrt n), and above them four-input merges MERGE4I whose pair fibers are streamed by class-restricted Schroeppel-Shamir heaps rather than stored as tables; free-frequency odd-part decoder, controlled-shift 2-adic part, explicit source cap, and exhaustive search for n < 1024; specified in full in proof.md) outputs the entire s with unconditional probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 from independent ideal coset copies, and on EVERY execution branch, including all failures, retries, discards and aborts, the total number Q(N,s) of fresh source copies acquired, counting every discarded, rejected and failed-attempt copy, is at most N(n+10) on the finite branch n < 1024 and at most the precomputed cap Qcap = O(n^(3/2) (log2 n) 2^((29/20) sqrt n)) on the main branch n >= 1024. Hence Q(N,s) = O(n^(3/2) (log2 n) 2^((29/20) sqrt n)), with envelope B_samples(n) = n^(3/2) (log2 n) 2^((29/20) sqrt n), whose exact growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N, s and outcomes. The inner coefficient 29/20 is an explicit rational, not an unknown big-O constant. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and the tolerance claim for the same execution.

For the same IFC1 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N >= 2 and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 > 2/3 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
